headline: CBA's net interest margin decreased 4 bps to 2.04% in 1H26 from 2.08% in 1H25 (cash basis). Excluding liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, underlying NIM was flat. The decline was driven by higher funding costs (-3 bps) from declining interest rates, unfavourable deposit mix and increased deposit price competition, and lower asset pricing (-2 bps) from home lending and business lending competition, partly offset by +6 bps from the replicating portfolio and equity hedges, +1 bps from favourable portfolio mix from strong at-call deposit growth, and -3 bps from Treasury & Markets due to higher funding costs in Carbon and Commodities and Global Markets and increased reverse repo balances. Liquids dragged -3 bps; basis risk was flat.

drivers.narrative: Growth in liquid assets (+$20bn) and institutional repos (+$10bn) had broadly neutral impacts on net interest income but dragged margin by 3 bps as reported in the NIM walk.
Home lending pricing down 2 bps and business lending pricing down 1 bps reflecting elevated competition, partly offset by higher consumer finance margins up 1 bps.
Driven by declining interest rates, unfavourable deposit mix and increased deposit price competition.
Favourable funding mix from strong growth in at-call deposits.
Flat — no material impact on margin.
Replicating portfolio contributed +5 bps from changes in portfolio rate and volume; higher earnings on capital hedges contributed +1 bps.
Higher funding costs in Carbon and Commodities and Global Markets (offset in other operating income), and an increase in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

limitations: The results book NIM walk includes 'Basis risk' as a separate bar at 0 bps, while the presentation slide combines this into 'Interest rate risk hedging' at +6 bps alongside the replicating portfolio. Both walks sum to -4 bps and agree on all other components.
Underlying NIM (ex-liquids) was flat per the bank's disclosure, meaning the -4 bps headline decline is entirely attributable to the liquidity drag.
No statutory-basis NIM figure is separately disclosed for comparison; the KPI table presents only the cash-basis measure.
Capped at 80: liquids -3 bps. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.

evidence_records.quote: [walk chart] NIM movement since December 2024: Dec 24 Half 208 -> Dec 25 Half 204

The Bank's net interest margin decreased 4 basis points on the prior comparative period to 2.04%. Excluding growth in liquid assets, which have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, net interest margin decreased by 1 basis point.

Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by home lending pricing (down 2 basis points) and business lending pricing (down 1 basis point) reflecting the impact of elevated competition, partly offset by higher consumer finance margins (up 1 basis point).
Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points driven by declining interest rates, unfavourable deposit mix and increased deposit price competition.
Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 1 basis point driven by favourable funding mix from strong growth in at-call deposits.

Capital, Replicating and Other: Increased margin by 6 basis points driven by the impact of the replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 5 basis points) and higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point).

Treasury and Markets: Decreased margin by 3 basis points due to higher funding costs in Carbon and Commodities and Global Markets (offset in other operating income), and an increase in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

Net Interest Income (NII) increased 6%, primarily driven by a $96 billion or 8% increase in Average Interest Earning Assets (AIEA), partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in Net Interest Margin (NIM). Excluding the impact of liquid assets and institutional reverse sale and repurchase agreements, the underlying NIM was unchanged.

Underlying NIM was primarily driven by higher earnings from the replicating portfolio and equity hedges, and favourable funding mix from strong growth in at-call deposits, offset by Treasury and Markets, the impact of declining interest rates, and increased deposit and lending price competition.
